column1: # switches.tsv: every switch the driver reads. Columns (tab separated): kind, name, tier, default, since, review, purpose.
# tools/switch_registry.py explains the columns and the rules; tools/test_switch_registry.py holds the tree to them.
# After merging work that adds or removes switches: python3 tools/switch_registry.py finalize
# A '#ceiling' only goes down. A '#pending' line marks a row written before its code was merged; finalize removes it.

column7: a variable of ANGLE (the GL layer of Chrome-family browsers), not of this driver: the plugin adds disableMetalOnNvidia to it, so that ANGLE draws with Metal on this card, and keeps what the process already had there. NVMTL_ANGLE_METAL=0 leaves it alone
a standard variable the driver reads
a host path: where the translator finds llvm-dis when one of its diagnostics runs it. The name is built from the tool's name
a host path: where the translator finds spirv-as when one of its diagnostics runs it. The name is built from the tool's name
a host path: where the translator finds spirv-val when one of its diagnostics runs it. The name is built from the tool's name
writes one JSON line of shader-compiler statistics per compiled shader stage on stderr (tools/nak-corpus, tools/nak_stats_diff.py); changes no code

Developer only (the video library's own override, in a process's environment or a line of the root-owned /usr/local/etc/nvencvt.conf): the library treats any card as an RTX 40, so on an RTX 50 it skips the decode self-test and registers every encoder and decoder untested on that card. Nothing sets it.

column4: on in Firefox's processes, plugin-container (NVENCVT_DEC_HOLD=0 in the environment or in /usr/local/etc/nvencvt.conf: every decoded picture is released when it is emitted, as in 3.0.4)
column7: In Firefox's processes (plugin-container) the video library's decoders keep each picture they emitted until eight later ones have been emitted, so that its pixel buffer is not handed out again and overwritten before Firefox's GPU process has taken the surface; other processes release it at once. From pull request 487 of the original project.

column4: on (NVK_BRIDGE_PRESENT_NEWEST=0 in the settings file: every swapchain of the native Vulkan frontend presents synchronously, on the application's thread, as in 3.0.8)
column7: An IMMEDIATE swapchain of the native Vulkan frontend, and since 3.0.11 a MAILBOX one (a mode that is offered only while this is on), hands each presented frame to a thread of the swapchain, which copies the newest one into a drawable when the layer has one, so vkQueuePresentKHR does not wait for the layer and a frame that was overtaken is not shown; the frontend reads the settings file alone, once, when a surface's present modes are first asked for or the process makes its first IMMEDIATE swapchain.

column4: on (NVK_CHANNEL_RECOVER=0 in the settings file: a channel fault ends the device, as in 2.9)
column7: After a GPU fault on one channel NVK rebuilds that channel and the application carries on, instead of losing its device.
NVK_DIAG=1: NVK's diagnostic lines, and the process's standard error goes to /private/tmp/nvk-diag-<pid>.log; a wait that times out dumps the state of every channel there

Test hook for the channel recovery: NVK_FAULT_INJECT=<mode>:<n>[:<process>] stalls or faults the n-th submission of a process once, so the rebuild can be watched. Set it in the settings file: a release plugin forgets it from the environment. Since 3.0.24 a development plugin also takes NVK_FAULT_INJECT=ws:<seconds>:<process>: that process runs WindowServer's crash-marker logic of the AIR-to-NIR road, its clean minute the seconds given (tools/air-nir/plugin-run.sh ws_marker); NVK has no mode ws and ignores it.

Keep CPU-written memory in system RAM: By default applications place the part of it the processor does not read back in video memory (faster in some games), while the desktop (WindowServer), memory shared between processes and what the processor reads back keep system RAM. On keeps all of it in system RAM in every application, as before 3.0.1; off places all of it in video memory, for the desktop too (unsafe for the desktop).

column4: on (NVK_ZCULL=0 in the settings file: NVK reports no ZCULL unit over NVRM and draws without hierarchical Z, as in 3.0.16)
column7: NVK's NVRM backend reports the GPU's ZCULL unit (NV2080_CTRL_CMD_GR_GET_ZCULL_INFO and the ZCULL context buffer's size), so NVK 26.3's hierarchical Z culls fragments hidden behind depth already drawn: in a render pass whose depth image is only a depth attachment and read, or whose depth is cleared at load. Off in WindowServer and with NVRM_610_ZCULL=0.
NVK_ZCULL_LOG=1 (or NVK_DIAG=1): one line on stderr per device with the ZCULL decision, the reason when it is off and RM's figures

column4: on (NVK_ZINK_OPACITY_KEEP=0 in the settings file: every OpenGL swap on Zink asks WindowServer for the drawable's opacity again, once, and sees an application's change at the next swap, as 3.0.7 did)
column7: A context of the Zink frontend keeps the answer to whether its drawable is opaque (kCGLCPSurfaceOpacity, a message to WindowServer and its reply) for 100 ms and asks again at once when the adapter sees its output change, so an application's own change of the opacity reaches the window up to 100 ms late; a swap asks at most once either way.

column4: on (NVK_ZINK_PRESENT_AHEAD=0 in the settings file: a swap waits for the GPU and publishes its frame itself, as in 3.0.6)
column7: An OpenGL swap on Zink hands its frame to a presentation thread of the process, which waits for the GPU, marks and tags the surface and presents the drawable; the swap returns at once, and the next swap waits for that frame first, so a context never has more than one frame on its way.

column4: on (NVK_ZINK_PRESENT_NEWEST=0 in the settings file: every OpenGL swap on Zink waits for the frame before it and asks the window's layer for its drawable itself, as in 3.0.9)
column7: An OpenGL swap on Zink with the swap interval at 0 leaves its frame parked in the context's scratch image and returns after waiting for the GPU alone; a sender thread asks the layer and hands over the frame that is parked when the layer answers, so an application is not held to the display and a frame that a newer one replaced first is never copied. It acts only while NVK_ZINK_PRESENT_AHEAD is on.

column4: on (NVK_ZINK_SUBDATA_STAGE=0 in the settings file: a glBufferSubData, or a glBufferData of the same size, that the threaded context would write through a mapping of a buffer the GPU may still be using waits for the GPU on the application's thread, as in 3.0.14)
column7: In OpenGL on Zink, a write of glBufferSubData (or of a glBufferData of the same size) that the threaded context would make through a synchronized mapping goes through a staging buffer instead, copied after every earlier call: a write of more than 320 bytes into a buffer the application has mapped and the GPU may still be using, and an unsynchronized write over the range of an earlier staging upload that is not executed yet. The application's thread no longer waits for the GPU there. A buffer of user memory, with CPU storage, in a client pointer heap, sparse or unmappable is never staged.

column4: on (NVK_ZINK_SURFACE_KEEP=0 in the settings file: the drawable's video memory is imported again for every frame, as in 3.0.6)
column7: The Zink frontend keeps its import of a drawable's video memory across frames (at most four surfaces per context) and names the block in every mark, which the kernel refuses when the surface has another block; it acts only while NVK_ZINK_PRESENT_AHEAD is on, and needs the kernel and the NVK of 3.0.7.

column4: on, WindowServer included since 3.0.24 (NVMTL_AIR_NIR=0 in the settings file: every compute and render pipeline is made from the translator's SPIR-V, as in 3.0.20)
column7: A compute pipeline is made from the NIR that NVK's own AIR-to-NIR frontend builds from the kernel's AIR, and a render pipeline from the NIR of both its stages (nvk/air, docs/AIR-TO-NIR.md), with the translator's SPIR-V as the fallback for a function the frontend refuses, a pipeline NVK will not make, a render pipeline that needs one of the SPIR-V road's rewrites of its stages, a dispatch with a pixel-coordinate sampler and a threadgroup size the road does not run; only with an NVK that has the frontend. A GPU fault in a process with pipelines on the road turns it off there, and in that process's next launches with the same driver build (the fallback list in the plugin's shader-cache folder); WindowServer is guarded besides by its crash marker.
NVK's AIR-to-NIR frontend says on standard error where a module's static initializer could not be run, for looking into a refusal

development plugins only (a release plugin ignores it): every function is made with the translator, as with NVMTL_AIR_NIR=0, and the plugin log compares the AIR-to-NIR frontend's reflection of it with the translator's, key by key, and its default threadgroup size with the SPIR-V's (docs/AIR-TO-NIR.md phase 4)
NVK's AIR-to-NIR frontend writes the module it read (after its passes) to the file named, for looking into a refusal
NVK's AIR-to-NIR frontend writes the module once the function constants are in to the file named, for looking into a refusal
Built-in per-application profiles: On by default; off turns every shipped per-application profile off.

column4: on (NVMTL_ARGBUF_ARRAYS=0: an argument-buffer member that is an array of textures, samplers or buffers gets one field, its first element, as in 3.0.5)
column7: An argument-buffer struct member that is an array of resource handles gets one [[id]] per element when a shader library is loaded, so a shader that indexes the array past its first element is translated instead of refused or reading the wrong handle.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_ASYNCUP_REAP=0: a finished asynchronous texture upload keeps its staging buffer and its place until its image is next written, read back or freed, as in 3.0.5)
column7: The staging buffer, the submission and the place of an asynchronous texture upload (NVMTL_ASYNC_TEX_UPLOAD) are given back at the next upload once the GPU has finished the copy, at most 16 per upload and without waiting, so textures that are uploaded once and then only sampled do not fill the 256 places and push later uploads onto the path that waits; never in WindowServer.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_ASYNC_TEX_UPLOAD=0 in the settings file: replaceRegion waits for its copy, as in 3.0)
column7: A texture region upload (replaceRegion) is submitted without waiting for the GPU, with its own staging buffer and command buffer, and is finished before the image is overwritten, read back or freed (nvmtl_tex_upload.h), in every process but WindowServer; =1 turns it on there too.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_BIND_CACHE=0: the index buffer, every vertex buffer, the topology and primitive restart are recorded before every draw, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A draw does not record again the index buffer, the vertex buffer bindings, the primitive topology or primitive restart that its Vulkan command buffer already holds; a fresh command buffer records everything, and whoever records behind the cache (a patch draw, DLSS) clears it; never in WindowServer.

column4: on (NVMTL_BLIT_READONLY=0: a buffer with a caller copy that a command buffer used only as a blit copy's source is copied back to the caller's memory at completion, as in 3.0.3)
column7: A buffer with a caller copy (newBufferWithBytesNoCopy pages the driver copies) that a command buffer used only as the source of copyFromBuffer:toBuffer: or copyFromBuffer:toTexture: is not copied back at completion; any other use in the command buffer still copies it back. From pull request 578 of the original project.

column4: on (NVMTL_BUSY_DONE_EARLY=0 in the settings file: the done tags and the holds go out at the end of the command buffer, after its scheduled report and its presentations: the done tags as in 2.9, the holds as in 3.0 before this switch)
column7: A command buffer that completed writes its surfaces' done tags and closes its surface fence holds before it reports scheduled or hands its drawables over, so WindowServer does not wait for an application that already finished.
Card for an application: With more than one card: 0 is the primary, 1 the second and so on (up to 7), for every application (1) or per application (Game=1,*=0).

column4: on (NVMTL_CB_LEAN=0: every command buffer makes its two handler dispatch groups up front and every -commandBuffer takes the queue class lock to find the capacity semaphore, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A command buffer makes its scheduled-handler and completed-handler dispatch groups when the first handler of each kind is dispatched, and a queue's capacity semaphore is made with the queue and read without the class lock; Apple's OpenGL renderer makes on the order of a hundred command buffers a frame.

column4: on (NVMTL_CVAR_PARALLEL=0: a compute kernel's threadgroup-size variant is compiled while the variant table's lock is held, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A compute kernel's threadgroup-size variant is compiled outside the process-wide variant lock and the table is looked at again before the result goes in, so a dispatch of another kernel on another thread does not wait for the compile; two threads that miss the same size at once both compile it and one copy is destroyed.

column4: on (NVMTL_CVAR_SEED=0: the pipeline newComputePipelineState compiles is unspecialized and the variant table starts empty, as in 3.0.5)
column7: The pipeline newComputePipelineState compiles, so that a kernel NVK cannot build is refused there, is specialized for the kernel's default threadgroup size and kept as that size's variant, so the first dispatch at that size does not compile the kernel a second time; a module whose size is not given by plain SpecId defaults stays unspecialized.

column4: on (NVMTL_DLSS_FG_SAME_IMAGE=0: Frame Generation records its priming evaluation whenever prevColorTexture is not the very texture object it last saw, as in 3.0.5)
column7: Frame Generation does not record the priming evaluation again when prevColorTexture is another texture (a view) for the image it handed the core at the last encode; only a different image, a reset or a missing history primes.

column4: on (NVMTL_DROP_REPORT=0 in the settings file: it is reported as completed, as in 2.9)
column7: A command buffer that was dropped while its channel was rebuilt is reported to the application as an error.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_DS_SKIP=0: setDepthStencilState applies the state again even when it is the one the encoder last applied, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A render encoder does not apply again a depth-stencil state that is the one it last applied; never in WindowServer.

column4: on (NVMTL_FC_REFUSAL_MEMO=0: every request for a function-constant variant goes to the translator, so the re-translate FAILED line and the NVMTL_FC_FAIL_DUMP and NVMTL_FC_DUMP_ALL files come back on every repeat, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A function-constant variant the translator refused is remembered for the process and answered with the same refusal without being translated again; the rest of the variant cache does not depend on it (NVMTL_FCCACHE_OFF turns the whole cache off, this memory included).
Frame-rate limit: One number for every application (60) or a list per application (Game=60,*=0). 10 to 1000; 0 is unlimited. Never applies to WindowServer.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_GL_FAST_FLUSH=0: commitAndWaitUntilSubmitted only waits for the submit-ahead thread or the worker, as in 3.0.5)
column7: commitAndWaitUntilSubmitted, which Apple's OpenGL renderer calls at every context flush, runs the submit-ahead step for its own queue on the committing thread, in order up to its own command buffer and with the same decisions, before it waits as before, instead of sleeping until another thread has taken the lock and submitted; never in WindowServer.

column4: on (NVMTL_GL_WAIT_EVENT=0: waitUntilComplete of a buffer or texture sleeps 50 us and looks again, as in 3.0.5)
column7: The OpenGL renderer's wait until no command buffer names a buffer or texture any more (waitUntilComplete, from GLDBufferRec::restoreData) sleeps on a condition that the release bringing the count to zero wakes, instead of polling every 50 us; the 10 s limit is the same.

column4: on (NVMTL_GSUB_HOST_READS=0: a part with any caller copy waits for the worker instead of being submitted ahead, as in 3.0.4)
column7: A part whose caller copies (newBufferWithBytesNoCopy pages the driver copies) are all buffers it only reads, and that no sealed part may have written, can be submitted ahead of the worker; one that a part may write still holds every later reader. From pull request 524 of the original project.
Low-latency mode (GPU work queued ahead): How many parts of GPU work may be queued ahead, 1 to 32 (default 16). A low number cuts input lag and can cost frame rate.

column4: on (NVMTL_IMAGE_GRACE=0 in the settings file: a released texture is freed at once, as in 2.9)
column7: A texture the application released keeps its memory until no command buffer that could still read it is open or in flight, so a late read is stale instead of a GPU fault.
A file path: the translator writes there the module its inline retry produced (the original project's 3.1 VFX fix), for reading a shader that still fails.

column4: on (NVMTL_MANAGED_SURFACE_TILED=0 in the settings file: a shader-writable Managed wrapper of a surface in the family's VRAM is drawn straight into the linear import, as in 3.0 before this switch)
column7: A shader-writable Managed wrapper of a single-plane surface in the family's VRAM is drawn, sampled and read by framebuffer fetch through a tiled image of its own, which is copied into the linear VRAM import before the surface is marked and from it when another writer made the VRAM newer.

column4: on for the cards known to decode correctly: RTX 30 and 40, and RTX 50 once its decode self-test has passed on the card (NVMTL_NVENCVT=0 in the settings file: never; 1: in every process, RTX 50 still behind its self-test)
column7: Hardware video decode and encode through the driver's own VideoToolbox service.

column4: on (NVMTL_PHOTOBOOTH_FLIP=0 in the settings file: Photo Booth's preview is shown as Core Image renders it into the drawable, as in 2.9)
column7: In Photo Booth only, the image Core Image renders into the preview's drawables is reflected within the rendered bounds, so the preview is upright; camera buffers, saved photos and other processes are not touched.

column4: on where each process's planar self-test saw every mark move the surface's seed by exactly one (NVMTL_PLANE_FOLLOW=0 in the settings file: marking one plane leaves the other planes' tags one seed behind, as in 3.0 before this switch)
column7: When the driver marks one plane of a surface whose planes sit in their own video memory, the other planes stay marked as current, so the frames WindowServer draws for a screen share are not locked, copied back and uploaded again at their next use. It acts only in a process whose self-test measured that a mark moves the surface's seed by exactly one; the log line 'planar surfaces: each of the self-test's ... marks' says so.

column4: on in games (NVMTL_PRETRANSLATE=0 in the settings file: shaders are translated when first asked for, as in 3.0)
column7: In a game (the games category or LSSupportsGameMode in its Info.plist) every entry point of a new shader library is translated ahead by a small low-priority pool and stored in the shader cache, so the first run of a level does not stop for each new shader; =1 turns it on in any process.

NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 in a process's own environment (exactly 1; not honoured in a process run as root or setuid/setgid): the release plugin keeps that process's driver variables (NVMTL_, NVK_, NVRM_ and the other driver prefixes), which then win over the settings file, and writes its log, /tmp/nvmtl.log, for that process, which it does for no other process

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_RES2_NOWAIT=0: a thread refused video memory polls up to 30 ms for the pager's pass and sleeps up to 16 ms for evicted memory to drain, with a 250 ms pause after a wait that ran out, and three Private buffers without a fallback are refused, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A thread that is refused video memory hands the residency pass to the pager's worker when the worker holds it, frees what has already drained without waiting and goes on to the system-memory fallback it took when the old waits ran out; the visibility accumulation scratch and the acceleration-structure user-ID tables, which had no fallback, retry in system memory; never in WindowServer.

column4: on (NVMTL_SCHEDULED_AFTER_SUBMIT=0: scheduled is reported before the part is handed to the queue, as in 3.0.4)
column7: A command buffer reports scheduled once the queue has accepted its part and the part's kernel fence is armed, not before the submission, so a scheduled handler that hands a surface to another process runs after something holds it. A command buffer whose first part is empty (one that begins with an event wait) still reports when that part is retired, as in 3.0.4. The worker's report after vkQueueSubmit is from pull request 524 of the original project; the same order in the submit-ahead pass and after the synchronous submit is this tree's.

column4: on (NVMTL_SCHEDULE_EARLY=0: a command buffer held until its surface writes are published reports scheduled only when it has finished, as in 3.0.4)
column7: A command buffer held until its surface writes are published reports scheduled as soon as they are, when a later part of it waits for an event (the iOS Simulator waits for one its scheduled handler leads to, and hung). From pull request 524 of the original project.

column4: on (NVMTL_SCHEDULE_SIMULATOR=0 in the settings file: SimMetalHost and SimRenderServer keep schedule mode 3, as in 3.0.4; no other process changes)
column7: The iOS Simulator's GPU processes, SimMetalHost and SimRenderServer, publish every surface write before they report scheduled (schedule mode 1, as the Chromium family does), so the simulated screen is not composed from a surface the GPU has not finished. An explicit NVMTL_SCHEDULE_AFTER_SURFACE_WRITES digit still wins. From pull request 524 of the original project (its part P5, which took a token of that setting instead).
Shader cache size limit (MB): Size at which the shader cache is trimmed (default 2048). 0 turns trimming off.

column4: on (NVMTL_SURFACE_VRAM_PIPE=0 in the settings file: the family VRAM import opens /dev/null with a plain open(), so a process whose sandbox refuses it, as Firefox's do, draws its surfaces through private images and copies, as in 3.0.4)
column7: A process whose sandbox refuses /dev/null (Firefox's) imports a surface's family VRAM with the read end of an empty pipe as its descriptor, as NVK's own opens there already do, instead of failing the import without a word; a process that may open /dev/null is not changed. From pull request 487 of the original project.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_SURFIN_SKIP_OWN_OUT=0: a bind of a surface texture waits on the surface's monitor for the copy-out in flight, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A command encoder's bind of a surface drawn through a private image does not wait for this process's own copy-out of that image to the surface's pages while it is in flight, unless a zero fill was lost or another writer has published into the surface's video memory meanwhile; CPU reads and writes of the texture still wait; never in WindowServer.

column4: on in WindowServer (NVMTL_SURFIN_ZERO=0: WindowServer uploads a surface whose pages are all zero and waits for the copy, as in 3.0)
column7: WindowServer does not upload a surface whose memory pages are all zero, such as the new surface of each captured frame of a shared screen: it clears the surface's video memory on the GPU ahead of its next command buffer instead of copying and waiting. Off with NVMTL_PRESUBMIT_PROLOGUE=0.

column4: on (NVMTL_SURFOUT_PLANES=0 in the settings file: each plane is copied out on its own, as in 2.9)
column7: The planes of a two-plane surface drawn through private images (the frames WindowServer draws for a screen share) are copied back to the surface together, under one lock and with one wait for the GPU, so the other plane is not uploaded again at its next use.

column4: on except in WindowServer (NVMTL_TEX_RECYCLE=0: every dead texture is destroyed and every new one created and allocated, as in 3.0.5)
column7: A dead ordinary colour texture of up to 32 MB keeps its Vulkan image and memory for at most a second, up to 32 images and 128 MB, and the next texture of the same format, size, mips, layers and usage takes them instead of four round trips to the kernel; they are given back first when video memory runs short; never in WindowServer, and never an image that was re-backed, migrated or sparse.

column4: on (NVMTL_UNIFORM_CBUF=0: GL and ANGLE uniforms stay in the address table, as in 3.0.3, where the promotion never ran)
column7: OpenGL (vs_uniform_buffer, fs_uniform_buffer) and ANGLE (ANGLE_userUniforms) uniform buffers that are only read are promoted to an NVK constant bank; it is on since 3.0.4 (pull requests 573, 579 and 580 of the original project). Also read from the settings file.

column4: on (NVMTL_WHOLE_VIEWS=0 in the settings file: the shader translator retypes a local variable through any pointer derived from it, a pointer-free local that a helper reads as bytes keeps its declared type, and a parameter read both as its members and as bytes keeps the type it first saw, as in 3.0.4)
column7: The shader translator retypes a local variable only through a pointer proven to address all of it, makes a pointer-free local that a helper reads as bytes one byte array of the local's size, and gives a pointer parameter read both as a pointer-free struct or array and as bytes one byte array of that size, so such shaders of League of Legends and of apps in the iOS Simulator translate instead of falling back (from pull request 524 of the original project). The plugin adds -wv0 to its shader cache tag when it is 0, so the two modes never share a cached module.

column4: on in WindowServer (NVMTL_WS_FREE_OFFMAIN=0: a released texture's import of video memory is freed by the thread that releases it, as in 3.0)
column7: WindowServer frees the video-memory import of a texture it released on a thread of its own, so its compositor does not wait for the resource manager.

column4: on (NVMTL_WS_NOCOPY_ONCE=0: in WindowServer, a newBufferWithBytesNoCopy range mapped read only and private is copied before each submission and written back after it, as in 3.0.4)
column7: WindowServer's newBufferWithBytesNoCopy ranges that the GPU cannot import and that are mapped read only, privately and with no file or device behind them are copied once when the buffer is made; the copy back into such pages faulted. From pull request 524 of the original project.

column4: on (NVMTL_XLATE_ADDR_RETRY=0: a shader the translator refuses for a select between two buffer roots is refused, as in 3.0.5; the plugin then adds -ar0 to its shader cache tag)
column7: A shader module the translator refused because a pointer is picked between two different buffers (a select or phi across buffer roots) is constructed again with device addresses for those buffers, as a last resort after every other attempt, instead of being refused.

column4: on (NVMTL_YUV422=0 in the settings file: 4:2:2 textures are refused, as in 2.9)
column7: Textures in the packed 4:2:2 video formats (BGRG422, GBGR422), which CoreVideo uses for camera frames, are created and sampled instead of refused.

NVRM_ASYNC=0 (any value that begins with 0) turns NVK's asynchronous submission off: each flush waits until the GPU has finished it, the waits and syncs between submissions do nothing and memory is freed at once, as before NVK's asynchronous path; channel recovery is off with it, and NVK's channels are not registered with the surface fence

column4: on (NVRM_EVENT_WAIT=0 in the settings file: every process polls, as 2.9's applications did; 2.9's WindowServer slept on the event)
column7: A thread that waits for the GPU sleeps until the kernel reports the GPU's event, after a spin whose length follows how long such waits take. 2.9 did this in WindowServer and in applications whose built-in profile asked for it.
NVRM_GSUB_LOG set to any value, 0 included: when a channel closes, NVK prints on standard error how its submissions and waits went (event sleeps, wakes, time-outs, fallbacks to polling)

column7: Start-up waits for what it needs (start finished, heads published, a head scanning) in short polls, each bounded by the time 2.9 slept, instead of sleeping fixed times.
